questionnaire.question: Can anyone register for access?
Are registrations vetted by a human prior to provisioning, or are they automatically granted if the criteria are met?
Can the same person or identity register multiple times?
Can users register for different roles or permissions?
What proof of identity is required for a registration to be successful?
Are registered identities verified?
Can identity information be easily forged or faked?
Can the exchange of identity information be manipulated during registration?
Is there any authorisation required before an account is provisioned?
Can accounts be provisioned with excessive privileges?
Can one user provision an account for another user without oversight?
Are provisioned accounts tied to a verified identity?
Is the provisioning process logged and auditable?
Is there a de-provisioning (offboarding) process, and is it enforced?
Are provisioning requests validated before execution?
Does the endpoint allow brute force? (No lockout / rate limiting observed after repeated failed attempts)
Are security questions easy to guess? (Weak, common, or user-enumerable answers accepted)
questionnaire.note: Evaluated regardless of Item_1 verdict. Y = indicator of compromise.

questionnaire.question: If brute force is allowed, is OTP code guessing present? (OTP endpoint lacks lockout)
Does the password policy enforce sufficient entropy (minimum length + character complexity: uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols)?
Can password history be bypassed? (e.g. cycle through N passwords so the Nth+1 reuse of the original is accepted)
questionnaire.note: Verdict semantics in the script: True = history enforced (bypass not possible).

questionnaire.question: Does the password expiry policy align with NIST SP 800-63B? (NIST recommends NO mandatory periodic expiry unless compromise is suspected)
Does the application maintain a history of the user's previous passwords to prevent reuse?
Does the policy reject passwords containing the user's first name, last name, or username?
Does the policy reject common/dictionary passwords? (Test with a set of common passwords)
